chunks: And from him, from Ayoub, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the slave who performs li'an with the free woman, he said: 'Yes, if his master married her to him and he performed li'an with the command of his master, that is so.'
And he said: 'There is li'an between the free man and the slave woman, and between the Muslim and the dhimmi woman.'
And it is also possible that the report came out as taqiyyah (dissimulation), because among the opponents there is one who says there is no li'an between the free man and the slave woman.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of li'an between a slave and a free woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that a slave’s capacity for li'an is contingent upon his master’s authority in arranging the marriage, distinguishing it from the independent status of free persons. It further extends the ruling to include Muslims and dhimmi women, while noting the scholarly debate on whether this inclusion reflects actual legal principle or was issued under taqiyyah to counter opposing views. This highlights the nuanced interplay between social hierarchy and judicial procedure in Shia fiqh.
